page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard CPU execution. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the average tier for multi-core operations, while single-core performance is relatively weak. The stress-ng multi-core CPU benchmark and Geekbench multi-core tests both register in the middle 50% of tested servers, whereas single-core stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is stable, with cached small-block reads reaching 781.7 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 86.1 GB/sec. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests, consistently perform within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6e.4xlarge offers dedicated compute resources without the overhead of bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, making it a resource-dense option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require high memory-to-CPU ratios. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio is optimized for compute-heavy applications. Suitable workloads include multi-threaded web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and general-purpose batch processing where multi-core scaling can offset the modest single-core performance.
